why: I compared the PASS and FAIL conditions of all seven verifier checks with the words of their expect lines. Checks 1–5 ask for the exact stdout plus one newline, and Check 1 also asks for exit=0. The expect lines say "prints exactly … followed by a newline", so the byte comparison with cmp is what the words require. Check 5 uses printf '%s\n', which keeps the JSON escape as a literal backslash-t, and that matches the words. Check 6's PASS asks for exit=0 and a test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab input and asserts on the output, which is exactly what the expect line says. Check 7 only asks that README mentions --tsv and shows an example command. The stricter extras are all under "Advisory": the mutation test, other flag positions, the README saying "tab-separated", and the test:cli mismatch. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond what the words require.
